title: AZ-900 · Describe Azure identity, access, and security · Describe defense-in-depth

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: Which statement best describes Defense in depth?

options.text: Protections for datacenter facilities and physical hardware
A protection approach that can reduce exposure by limiting management-port access to approved time windows
Using identity and device state with tools such as Intune and Conditional Access
A security strategy that uses multiple layers so the failure of one control does not expose the entire system

questions.explanation: Defense in depth is a security strategy that uses multiple layers so the failure of one control does not expose the entire system.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: In the context of this Microsoft Learn unit, what does Physical security layer refer to?

options.text: Technology that synchronizes identities between on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID
Protections for datacenter facilities and physical hardware
Identity synchronization from Microsoft Entra ID to Microsoft Entra Domain Services without syncing managed-domain-only objects back
Reassessing trust based on changing signals rather than assuming a one-time login establishes permanent trust

questions.explanation: Physical security layer is protections for datacenter facilities and physical hardware.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: Which description correctly matches Identity and access layer?

options.text: Verifying the identity of a person, service, or device before granting access
Something the user is, such as a fingerprint or facial biometric
A Conditional Access control that permits access only from devices meeting compliance requirements
Controls that verify identities and restrict permissions

questions.explanation: Identity and access layer is controls that verify identities and restrict permissions.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: Which of the following is the best definition of Perimeter layer?

options.text: A hardware-based passwordless authentication option supported by Microsoft Entra ID
Controls that protect the boundary from external network threats
Supporting sign-in experiences for customers who use an organization’s applications
Information about the requesting user or workload used to evaluate access

questions.explanation: Perimeter layer is controls that protect the boundary from external network threats.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: What is the primary meaning of Network layer in Azure fundamentals?

options.text: Microsoft cloud-based identity and access management service
Segmentation and network controls that restrict communication paths
The identity or group membership used as part of a Conditional Access decision
An identity belonging to a person outside the organization who needs controlled access to applications or resources

questions.explanation: Network layer is segmentation and network controls that restrict communication paths.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: Select the TWO statements that are correct according to this unit.

options.text: Defense in depth: a security strategy that uses multiple layers so the failure of one control does not expose the entire system.
Identity and access layer: Microsoft cloud-based identity and access management service.
Defense in depth: controls that protect the boundary from external network threats.
Physical security layer: protections for datacenter facilities and physical hardware.
Physical security layer: secure coding, patching, and application-specific protections.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Defense in depth — a security strategy that uses multiple layers so the failure of one control does not expose the entire system; and Physical security layer — protections for datacenter facilities and physical hardware.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: Which TWO statements accurately reflect the concepts covered in this unit?

options.text: Perimeter layer: controls that protect the boundary from external network threats.
Identity and access layer: controls that verify identities and restrict permissions.
Perimeter layer: using overlapping safeguards so attackers must defeat multiple independent controls.
Perimeter layer: verifying the identity of a person, service, or device before granting access.
Identity and access layer: protections for virtual machines, containers, operating systems, and workloads.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Identity and access layer — controls that verify identities and restrict permissions; and Perimeter layer — controls that protect the boundary from external network threats.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: Select TWO correct statements about the material in this Microsoft Learn unit.

options.text: Network layer: using one identity sign-in to access multiple trusted applications.
Compute layer: verifying the identity of a person, service, or device before granting access.
Compute layer: protections for virtual machines, containers, operating systems, and workloads.
Network layer: segmentation and network controls that restrict communication paths.
Network layer: controls such as encryption and access restrictions applied directly to information.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Network layer — segmentation and network controls that restrict communication paths; and Compute layer — protections for virtual machines, containers, operating systems, and workloads.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: Which TWO statements are consistent with the unit content?

options.text: Data layer: controls such as encryption and access restrictions applied directly to information.
Compute layer: Microsoft Entra capabilities for integrating and controlling access to cloud and on-premises applications.
Data layer: Microsoft Entra capabilities for integrating and controlling access to cloud and on-premises applications.
Application layer: Microsoft cloud-based identity and access management service.
Application layer: secure coding, patching, and application-specific protections.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Application layer — secure coding, patching, and application-specific protections; and Data layer — controls such as encryption and access restrictions applied directly to information.

options.text: Application layer: using identity and device state with tools such as Intune and Conditional Access.
Defense in depth: protections for virtual machines, containers, operating systems, and workloads.
Layered mitigation: using overlapping safeguards so attackers must defeat multiple independent controls.
Defense in depth: a security strategy that uses multiple layers so the failure of one control does not expose the entire system.
Layered mitigation: using one identity sign-in to access multiple trusted applications.
